argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean certification. It supports certification for aggregate launch readiness because the release clears aggregate readiness by 2.1 percentage points, had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and passed general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same record also shows deferred-defect routing is a named deployment context with no completed evaluation coverage, so that area remains unknown rather than passed. The supportable packet is therefore certification with an explicit disclosed limitation or evaluation-gap caveat, not a clean claim of no known limitations for the maintenance triage context.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to justify the position. The narrower request is based on risk-weighted interpretation of the admissible record, not on schedule pressure.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy in the admissible record does not require treating the whole launch as failed merely because one named context lacks coverage; it requires disclosure or resolution of material limitations and evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts before clean certification. The policy concern is overstatement. A packet that certifies overall readiness while expressly stating that deferred-defect routing remains an unresolved evaluation gap is consistent with the policy text and with the model-card and risk-management guidance cited in the record. What is not supportable is any implication that the named context has passed or that there are no known limitations.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show the actual certification artifact or model-card text containing the required disclosure.
The current admissible record does not show an approved risk-acceptance record.
Clean certification with no deployment limitation for the named maintenance triage context is not supportable on this record.
Deferred-defect routing must be treated as unknown rather than passed.
